      - reporting year

  - name: Compliance Status
    expr: CASE WHEN evidence_datetime IS NOT NULL THEN 'MET' ELSE 'NOT_MET' END
    comment: "Computed live: MET = an A1c test exists in the measurement year; NOT_MET\

    display_name: Compliance Status

      - adherence status
      - gap status

      - site
      - location
      - facility

  - name: Panel
    expr: panel_id
    comment: PCP panel the patient belongs to.
    display_name: Panel
    synonyms:
      - panel
      - pcp panel
      - provider panel
      - care team

  - name: Gap Reason
    expr: CASE WHEN evidence_datetime IS NOT NULL THEN 'Met' ELSE 'No A1c test in

    comment: "Computed live: why the patient is a care gap (NOT_MET); 'Met' when compliant.\

      - gap reason
      - reason
      - care gap reason

    synonyms:
      - age group
      - age bracket

      - eligible population
      - eligible count
      - patients eligible

  - name: Compliant Patients
    expr: COUNT(1) FILTER (WHERE evidence_datetime IS NOT NULL)

Effective **measurement year 2026**, the Glycemic Status Assessment (GSD) numerator accepts a **Glucose
Management Indicator (GMI)** derived from continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) as an equivalent glycemic-status
result, alongside a laboratory **HbA1c**. The GMI result is identified by **LOINC 97506-0**; HbA1c remains
**LOINC 4548-4** (and method variants). A patient with a qualifying GMI but no lab HbA1c is now **compliant**.
Operational impact: the GSD value set gains a code for MY2026. A patient who looked like a care gap under the
MY2025 value set (CGM data only, no lab draw) flips to compliant under MY2026 — a pure **measure-drift** event
driven by a value-set version change, not by any change in the patient's data.

- Check HbA1c **every 3 months** for patients who are above individualized goal or whose therapy has changed.
- Check HbA1c **every 6 months** for patients who are stable at goal.
- Do not react to a single out-of-range HbA1c; confirm with a repeat before escalating therapy.
The GSD measure requires only **one** A1c in the measurement year, so it cannot distinguish a patient checked
quarterly from one checked once.

A single population A1c threshold is **not** appropriate for every adult with diabetes. The target range is
individualized by comorbidity burden and life expectancy:
| Patient profile | Target A1c range |
|---|---|
| No or minimal microvascular complications, >10 years life expectancy | 6.0–7.0% |
| Moderate comorbidity, 5–10 years life expectancy | 7.0–8.0% |
| Marked comorbidity or end-stage disease, <5 years life expectancy | 8.0–9.0% |
This is the key difference from the GSD quality **measure**, which only records whether an A1c test happened
and buckets the latest value as good control (<8.0%) or poor control (>9.0%). The measure answers *"was a test
done and what was the value?"*; the protocol answers *"what should this specific patient's target be?"*.

For **MY2026**, the eGFR value set is modernized to the race-free CKD-EPI 2021 estimating equation and
**drops the legacy race-based (MDRD) eGFR code** that older lab feeds still emit. Health systems whose result
feed still carries the legacy code will see eGFR coverage — and therefore KED compliance — fall on otherwise
unchanged data until mapping is updated. This is the second controlled drift scenario in the demo.

Measure Eligible ages Numerator (compliant when…) Threshold / definition GSD — Glycemic Status Assessment 18–75 ≥1 HbA1c test in the measurement year Good control < 8.0%; poor control > 9.0%; general target < 7.0% KED — Kidney Health Evaluation 18–85 BOTH an eGFR test AND a uACR test in the year Both components required; either alone is a gap BPD — Blood Pressure Control 18–75 Most recent BP reading controlled Controlled = systolic < 140 mmHg AND diastolic < 90 mmHg SPD — Statin Therapy 40–75 Dispensed a statin during the year Moderate-to-high intensity statin EED — Eye Exam 18–75 Retinal / diabetic eye exam in the year Dilated or retinal-imaging exam; biennial if prior exam normal and low risk A1c is identified by LOINC Component "Hemoglobin A1c" across methods (e.g. 4548-4 default, 17856-6 HPLC, 59261-8 IFCC). eGFR and uACR are the two required kidney components of KED.

Ontology Page — Compliance Rate [Clinical Domain]: Aggregate measure metric: compliant ÷ eligible patients, exposed as a governed measure in each *_compliance_metrics metric view.
## Definition
**Compliance rate = compliant (numerator) ÷ eligible (denominator)** for a measure in a measurement year.

## Data
| Measure | Metric view | Governed metrics |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GSD | `gsd_compliance_metrics` | GSD Compliance Rate |
| KED | `ked_compliance_metrics` | KED Compliance Rate, eGFR Test Rate, uACR Test Rate |
| EED | `eed_compliance_metrics` | EED compliance |
| BPD | `bpd_compliance_metrics` | BPD compliance |
| SPD | `spd_compliance_metrics` | SPD compliance |

## Business use
Use the governed metric instead of recomputing the ratio. A rate change can come from a change in care or from a change in the definition; check **Measure Drift** before reading a change as a change in care.

    expr: measurement_year
    comment: HEDIS measurement year the metrics are computed for (e.g. 2026).
    display_name: Measurement Year
    synonyms:
      - year
      - reporting year
      - MY

  - name: Compliance Status
    expr: CASE WHEN egfr_datetime IS NOT NULL AND uacr_datetime IS NOT NULL THEN 'MET'
      ELSE 'NOT_MET' END
    comment: "Computed live: MET = both an eGFR and a uACR test were found in the\
      \ measurement year; NOT_MET = at least one is missing."
    display_name: Compliance Status
    synonyms:
      - status
      - met status
      - adherence status
      - gap status

  - name: Clinic
    expr: clinic_id
    comment: Clinic (site) the patient's panel belongs to. Enables care-gap and compliance
      rates by site.
    display_name: Clinic
    synonyms:
      - clinic
      - site
      - location
      - facility

  - name: Panel
    expr: panel_id
    comment: PCP panel the patient belongs to.
    display_name: Panel
    synonyms:
      - panel
      - pcp panel
      - provider panel
      - care team

  - name: Gap Reason
    expr: CASE WHEN egfr_datetime IS NOT NULL AND uacr_datetime IS NOT NULL THEN 'Met'
      WHEN egfr_datetime IS NULL AND uacr_datetime IS NULL THEN 'No eGFR or uACR test'
      WHEN egfr_datetime IS NULL THEN 'No eGFR test' ELSE 'No uACR test' END
    comment: "Computed live: why the patient is a care gap (NOT_MET); 'Met' when compliant.\
      \ Group care gaps by reason."
    display_name: Gap Reason
    synonyms:
      - gap reason
      - reason
      - care gap reason
      - why gap

  - name: Age Band
    expr: CASE WHEN age < 45 THEN '18-44' WHEN age < 65 THEN '45-64' ELSE '65-85'
      END
    comment: Age band at the end of the measurement year (KED eligible population
      is 18-85).
    display_name: Age Band
    synonyms:
      - age group
      - age bracket
      - age range

  - name: Measure
    expr: measure_id
    comment: HEDIS measure code; this view reports KED (Kidney Health Evaluation).
    display_name: HEDIS Measure
    synonyms:
      - measure id
      - hedis measure
      - quality measure

measures:
  - name: Eligible Patients
    expr: COUNT(1)
    comment: Diabetes patients aged 18-85 eligible for KED (the measure denominator).
      One row per patient.
    display_name: Eligible Patients
    format:
      type: number
      decimal_places:
        type: exact
        places: 0
    synonyms:
      - denominator
      - eligible population
      - eligible count
      - patients eligible

  - name: eGFR Tested Patients
    expr: COUNT(1) FILTER (WHERE egfr_datetime IS NOT NULL)
    comment: Eligible patients with at least one eGFR (estimated glomerular filtration
      rate) test in the measurement year.
    display_name: eGFR Tested Patients
    format:
      type: number
      decimal_places:
        type: exact
        places: 0
    synonyms:
      - egfr tested
      - gfr tested
      - kidney function tested
      - egfr count

  - name: uACR Tested Patients
    expr: COUNT(1) FILTER (WHERE uacr_datetime IS NOT NULL)
    comment: Eligible patients with at least one uACR (urine albumin-creatinine ratio)
      test in the measurement year.
    display_name: uACR Tested Patients
    format:
      type: number
      decimal_places:
        type: exact
        places: 0
    synonyms:
      - uacr tested
      - urine albumin tested
      - microalbumin tested
      - uacr count

  - name: Compliant Patients
    expr: COUNT(1) FILTER (WHERE egfr_datetime IS NOT NULL AND uacr_datetime IS NOT
      NULL)
    comment: "Eligible patients meeting the full KED numerator: BOTH an eGFR and a\
      \ uACR test in the measurement year — computed live."
    display_name: Compliant Patients
    format:
      type: number
      decimal_places:
        type: exact
        places: 0
    synonyms:
      - numerator
      - compliant count
      - patients met
      - both tests
      - complete kidney eval

  - name: KED Compliance Rate
    expr: MEASURE(`Compliant Patients`) / MEASURE(`Eligible Patients`)
    comment: Share of eligible diabetes patients with BOTH an eGFR and a uACR test
      in the measurement year. Numerator / denominator; re-aggregates at any grain.
    display_name: KED Compliance Rate
    format:
      type: percentage
      decimal_places:
        type: max
        places: 1
    synonyms:
      - compliance rate
      - adherence rate
      - ked rate
      - kidney eval rate
      - met rate

  - name: eGFR Test Rate
    expr: MEASURE(`eGFR Tested Patients`) / MEASURE(`Eligible Patients`)
    comment: Share of eligible patients with an eGFR test. Component of the KED numerator.
    display_name: eGFR Test Rate
    format:
      type: percentage
      decimal_places:
        type: max
        places: 1
    synonyms:
      - egfr rate
      - gfr test rate

  - name: uACR Test Rate
    expr: MEASURE(`uACR Tested Patients`) / MEASURE(`Eligible Patients`)
    comment: Share of eligible patients with a uACR test. Component of the KED numerator;
      typically the limiting component.
    display_name: uACR Test Rate
    format:
      type: percentage
      decimal_places:
        type: max
        places: 1
    synonyms:
      - uacr rate
      - urine albumin rate

Table eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.icd10_closure: Transitive closure of icd10_hier; select a whole subtree with one equality (WHERE ancestor_code=X). Built once by build_closure.py.
Columns: ancestor_code (ICD-10-CM code of the ancestor (broader) concept, e.g. E11 (Type 2 diabetes mellitus).); ancestor_name (Name of the ancestor concept.); descendant_code (ICD-10-CM code of the descendant (narrower) concept, e.g. E11.21. A single equality join on this column subsumes the whole subtree.); descendant_name (Name of the descendant concept.); depth (Hierarchy distance from ancestor to descendant (0 = self). Enables subsumption queries without recursive CTEs.)

Table eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.icd10_hier: ICD-10-CM adjacency list (code, parent_code, name). Source tree for icd10_closure. Curated demo subset (diabetes), ADR-0007.
Columns: code (ICD-10-CM code of this concept (the child node of a direct parent/child edge).); parent_code (ICD-10-CM code of the immediate parent concept. Direct edges only; transitively expanded (all depths) into icd10_closure.); name (Human-readable name of the ICD-10-CM concept.)

Table eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.loinc: LOINC code subset (loinc_code, long_common_name, concept) for demo measures: A1c, eGFR, uACR, BP, BMI, PHQ. LOINC (c) Regenstrief, used under LOINC License.
Columns: loinc_code (LOINC code (e.g. 4548-4 = Hemoglobin A1c / HbA1c in blood).); long_common_name (LOINC long common name for the lab test.); concept (Short semantic concept label grouping related LOINC codes (e.g. A1C, EGFR, UACR, BP).)

Table eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.loinc_parts: LOINC multiaxial Part edges (loinc_code, predicate, part): typed axes has_component/has_system/has_method. A graph (not a tree): 'all A1c regardless of method' = terms sharing Component LP-HBA1C. Curated demo subset (LOINC License), ADR-0010.
Columns: loinc_code (LOINC code being decomposed into its semantic Parts (e.g. 4548-4 Hemoglobin A1c).); loinc_name (LOINC long common name of the code.); predicate (LOINC Part axis / relationship: has_component, has_system, has_method, etc.); part (LOINC Part code on the object side of the predicate (e.g. LP-HBA1C, LP-SYS-BLD).); part_name (Human-readable Part name. Enables semantic grouping of labs across code vintages/methods (e.g. all HbA1c components regardless of method).)

Table eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.protocol_edges: Care-protocol knowledge edges (subject, predicate, object, value) from the care-protocol PDF: recommendedFor/contraindicatedWith/monitoredBy/hasThreshold. The clinical, cross-vocabulary relationships for the graph (OWL/Ontobricks) and class-6 multi-hop questions. ADR-0010.
Columns: subject (Subject of a care-protocol edge, typically a drug class (e.g. DRUGCLASS-STATIN, DRUGCLASS-SGLT2, DRUGCLASS-ACE).); predicate (Edge relationship: recommendedFor, firstLineFor, contraindicatedWith, or contraindicatedWhen.); object (Object of the edge: a measure, condition, comorbidity, or contraindication (e.g. SPD, ALBUMINURIA, COMORBID_CKD, CONTRA_PREGNANCY, eGFR_LT_30).); value (Optional numeric threshold attached to the edge (e.g. 30 for eGFR_LT_30); null when not applicable.); source (Citation into the care-protocol document (section/version, e.g. CP-DM-2025.1 sec2). Record-level provenance for the recommendation.)

Table eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.rxnorm_closure: Transitive closure of rxnorm_hier; select a whole subtree with one equality (WHERE ancestor_code=X). Built once by build_closure.py.
Columns: ancestor_code (RxNorm ingredient rxcui (e.g. 36567 simvastatin). Join a value set of ingredients here to subsume all clinical drugs.); ancestor_name; descendant_code (RxNorm clinical-drug rxcui (e.g. 312961 Simvastatin 20 MG) subsumed by the ingredient, matching prescription codes in bronze_order_med.); descendant_name; depth

Table eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.rxnorm_hier: RxNorm adjacency (code, parent_code, name): statin ingredient -> clinical drug. Source tree for rxnorm_closure, so SPD resolves ingredient value sets to the clinical-drug codes actually prescribed (subsumption). Curated demo subset, ADR-0007.
Columns: code (RxNorm rxcui of this concept (child node of the edge), typically a clinical drug.); parent_code (RxNorm rxcui of the immediate parent concept (e.g. the ingredient). Transitively expanded into rxnorm_closure.); name (Human-readable RxNorm concept name.)

Table eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.rxnorm_statin: RxNorm statin ingredients (rxcui, ingredient) for the Statin Therapy (SPD) measure.
Columns: rxcui (RxNorm ingredient rxcui for a statin (e.g. 36567 simvastatin). Joined to rxnorm_closure to subsume every statin clinical drug for the SPD numerator.); ingredient (Statin ingredient name (e.g. simvastatin, atorvastatin).)

Table eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.value_set_segment: Cross-branch demo value sets / cohorts (the segment table; not NCQA/VSAC). Named sets spanning the hierarchy, incl. CARDIORENAL_COHORT (diabetes+CKD+HF).
Columns: segment_id (Value-set segment identifier, e.g. GSD_A1C_TEST (A1c lab codes), KED_EGFR, SPD_STATIN.); segment_name (Human-readable value-set name.); code (A member code of the value set (LOINC, ICD-10-CM, or RxNorm depending on code_system).); code_system (Terminology the code belongs to: LOINC, ICD10CM, or RXNORM.); measurement_year (HEDIS measurement year the value-set version applies to (drift demo: value sets change across years).); owner (Steward/owner of the value-set segment.)

CP-ESC-1 (statin gap). A patient aged 40–75 with diabetes and no statin dispensed in the year (SPD gap) should be started on a moderate-to-high intensity statin , after confirming no contraindication (pregnancy, active hepatic disease). CP-ESC-2 (kidney gap). A patient missing eGFR or uACR (KED gap) should have the missing component ordered. If uACR ≥ 30 mg/g, start an ACE inhibitor or ARB (not both). CP-ESC-3 (combined cardiorenal). A patient with diabetes and chronic kidney disease (N18.*) and heart failure (I50.*) is a cardiorenal priority: ensure statin, ACE/ARB, and an SGLT2 inhibitor (if eGFR ≥ 20), and monitor A1c every 3 months. Escalation rules reference measures (GSD/KED/SPD), labs (eGFR, uACR, A1c), diagnosis families (E10/E11/E13, N18, I50) and drug classes — the relationships this protocol contributes to the knowledge graph.

These agents are indicated for **cardiorenal protection even when A1c is already at goal**:
- Type 2 diabetes **plus atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD)**: add a GLP-1 RA or an SGLT2
  inhibitor to reduce major adverse cardiovascular events.
- Type 2 diabetes **plus heart failure**: add an **SGLT2 inhibitor** to reduce heart-failure hospitalization.
- Type 2 diabetes **plus chronic kidney disease** (eGFR ≥ 20): add an **SGLT2 inhibitor** for renal protection.
The decision is **outcome-driven, not glucose-driven**: a patient at an A1c goal on metformin alone who has
CKD with albuminuria should still have an SGLT2 inhibitor added for renal protection — a recommendation no
HEDIS quality measure captures.

Measure Eligible ages Numerator (compliant when…) Threshold / definition GSD — Glycemic Status Assessment 18–75 ≥1 HbA1c test in the measurement year Good control < 8.0%; poor control > 9.0%; general target < 7.0% KED — Kidney Health Evaluation 18–85 BOTH an eGFR test AND a uACR test in the year Both components required; either alone is a gap BPD — Blood Pressure Control 18–75 Most recent BP reading controlled Controlled = systolic < 140 mmHg AND diastolic < 90 mmHg SPD — Statin Therapy 40–75 Dispensed a statin during the year Moderate-to-high intensity statin EED — Eye Exam 18–75 Retinal / diabetic eye exam in the year Dilated or retinal-imaging exam; biennial if prior exam normal and low risk A1c is identified by LOINC Component "Hemoglobin A1c" across methods (e.g. 4548-4 default, 17856-6 HPLC, 59261-8 IFCC). eGFR and uACR are the two required kidney components of KED.

A single population A1c threshold is **not** appropriate for every adult with diabetes. The target range is
individualized by comorbidity burden and life expectancy:
| Patient profile | Target A1c range |
|---|---|
| No or minimal microvascular complications, >10 years life expectancy | 6.0–7.0% |
| Moderate comorbidity, 5–10 years life expectancy | 7.0–8.0% |
| Marked comorbidity or end-stage disease, <5 years life expectancy | 8.0–9.0% |
This is the key difference from the GSD quality **measure**, which only records whether an A1c test happened
and buckets the latest value as good control (<8.0%) or poor control (>9.0%). The measure answers *"was a test
done and what was the value?"*; the protocol answers *"what should this specific patient's target be?"*.

This protocol governs quality measurement and care escalation for adults with diabetes mellitus , identified by an ICD-10-CM diagnosis in the E10 (type 1), E11 (type 2), or E13 (other specified) families, including all descendant codes (e.g. E11.21 Type 2 diabetes with diabetic nephropathy , E11.319 … with unspecified diabetic retinopathy ). Membership is by the diagnosis hierarchy, not an enumerated code list.

FROM (
  SELECT DISTINCT d.patient_id
  FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.bronze_pat_enc_dx d
  INNER JOIN (
    SELECT DISTINCT patient_id

  ) k ON d.patient_id = k.patient_id
  WHERE d.icd10_code LIKE 'E10%' OR d.icd10_code LIKE 'E11%' OR d.icd10_code LIKE 'E13%'
) t

The diabetes cohort is defined by subsumption over the ICD-10-CM hierarchy, specifically diagnoses under E10, E11, and E13. Use this governed cohort definition when interpreting any of the five measure populations. Do not infer diabetes eligibility from unrelated diagnosis codes or from measure status alone.

Inferred snippet (business_logic) from Query history for eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.bronze_order_med and eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.rxnorm_closure: The target population consists of distinct patients with diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and heart failure diagnoses.
The clinical cohort is the set of DISTINCT `patient_id` values appearing in `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.bronze_pat_enc_dx` under all three diagnosis conditions: `icd10_code LIKE 'E11%' OR icd10_code LIKE 'E10%' OR icd10_code LIKE 'E13%'` for diabetes, `icd10_code LIKE 'N18%'` for chronic kidney disease, and `icd10_code LIKE 'I50%'` for heart failure. The three diagnosis subsets are joined with INNER JOIN on `patient_id`, so a patient must have at least one matching diagnosis in each subset. The cohort count is `COUNT(*)` over the resulting distinct patient list, not a count of diagnosis records.

Inferred snippet (business_logic) from (Clone) [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev): Diabetes quality reporting in this agent covers five HEDIS-aligned demo measures and is not NCQA-certified.
This Genie Agent covers five diabetes quality measures: GSD, KED, BPD, SPD, and EED. The measures are described as HEDIS-aligned demo content and explicitly are not NCQA-certified. The diabetes cohort is defined by subsumption over the ICD-10-CM hierarchy, using diagnoses under `E10`, `E11`, and `E13`. Analysts should treat these rules as the measure universe for this semantic layer rather than as certified HEDIS specifications.

Inferred snippet (business_logic) from (Clone) [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev): Kidney Health Evaluation requires both kidney tests for eligible diabetic patients aged 18–85, with uACR usually limiting completion.
KED means Kidney Health Evaluation for diabetic patients aged 18-85. A patient meets KED only when BOTH kidney tests are present: an eGFR test and a uACR test, represented by the KED numerator. The governed metric view supports `MEASURE(`KED Compliance Rate`)`, `MEASURE(`eGFR Test Rate`)`, and `MEASURE(`uACR Test Rate`)`; use these measures from `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.ked_compliance_metrics` when comparing KED overall compliance with the two components. The curated instruction notes that uACR is usually the limiting component, so questions about closing the KED gap often focus on missing uACR.

Inferred snippet (business_logic) from (Clone) [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev): Eye Exam measures whether eligible diabetic patients aged 18–75 had a retinal or diabetic eye exam during the year.
EED means Eye Exam for diabetic patients aged 18-75. A patient meets EED when they had a retinal or diabetic eye exam in the measurement year, represented by `gold_adherence_eed.numerator_flag`. The standard patient-level EED compliance formula is `COUNT_IF(gold_adherence_eed.numerator_flag) / COUNT(*)`, where the denominator is all EED-eligible rows at the grouping grain. Use `MEASURE(`EED Compliance Rate`)` from `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.eed_compliance_metrics` for governed rate reporting.

Ontology Page — Diabetes Cohort [Clinical Domain]: Patients with any ICD-10-CM diagnosis under E10, E11, or E13 (including all child codes); the base population for every diabetes measure.
## Definition
The set of patients with a diabetes diagnosis: any ICD-10-CM code that is a **descendant of E10, E11, or E13** (type 1, type 2, and other/specified diabetes).

## How it is resolved
The cohort is resolved semantically, not from a hand-maintained code list. `silver_condition` is joined to `icd10_closure` on `descendant_code` where `ancestor_code IN ('E10','E11','E13')`. One equality join captures the whole subtree (e.g. `E11.21`, `E11.319`); see **Code Subsumption**.

## Data
`silver_diabetes_cohort`: one row per distinct `patient_id`.

## Business use
All five diabetes measures apply their own age band to this cohort. A flat code list would miss specific child codes and undercount every measure.

CP-ESC-1 (statin gap). A patient aged 40–75 with diabetes and no statin dispensed in the year (SPD gap) should be started on a moderate-to-high intensity statin , after confirming no contraindication (pregnancy, active hepatic disease). CP-ESC-2 (kidney gap). A patient missing eGFR or uACR (KED gap) should have the missing component ordered. If uACR ≥ 30 mg/g, start an ACE inhibitor or ARB (not both). CP-ESC-3 (combined cardiorenal). A patient with diabetes and chronic kidney disease (N18.*) and heart failure (I50.*) is a cardiorenal priority: ensure statin, ACE/ARB, and an SGLT2 inhibitor (if eGFR ≥ 20), and monitor A1c every 3 months. Escalation rules reference measures (GSD/KED/SPD), labs (eGFR, uACR, A1c), diagnosis families (E10/E11/E13, N18, I50) and drug classes — the relationships this protocol contributes to the knowledge graph.

Measure Eligible ages Numerator (compliant when…) Threshold / definition GSD — Glycemic Status Assessment 18–75 ≥1 HbA1c test in the measurement year Good control < 8.0%; poor control > 9.0%; general target < 7.0% KED — Kidney Health Evaluation 18–85 BOTH an eGFR test AND a uACR test in the year Both components required; either alone is a gap BPD — Blood Pressure Control 18–75 Most recent BP reading controlled Controlled = systolic < 140 mmHg AND diastolic < 90 mmHg SPD — Statin Therapy 40–75 Dispensed a statin during the year Moderate-to-high intensity statin EED — Eye Exam 18–75 Retinal / diabetic eye exam in the year Dilated or retinal-imaging exam; biennial if prior exam normal and low risk A1c is identified by LOINC Component "Hemoglobin A1c" across methods (e.g. 4548-4 default, 17856-6 HPLC, 59261-8 IFCC). eGFR and uACR are the two required kidney components of KED.

**Statins and ACE inhibitors / ARBs are contraindicated in pregnancy.** A gap-closure recommendation that
would otherwise fire (e.g. "start a statin for this 40-year-old with diabetes") must be suppressed if the
patient is pregnant. This is an exclusion the structured measure does not reason about on its own.

Medication prescribing for patients with cardiovascular diagnoses is computed by joining event rows to encounters and diagnoses: `fact_clinical_event ce JOIN dim_medication m ON ce.medication_key = m.medication_key JOIN fact_encounter fe ON ce.encounter_key = fe.encounter_key JOIN dim_diagnosis dx ON fe.primary_diagnosis_key = dx.diagnosis_key`. The standard cardiovascular prescription cohort INCLUDES `dx.diagnosis_category = 'Cardiovascular' AND ce.event_type = 'Medication'`. The metric is `COUNT(*) AS prescription_count` grouped by `m.generic_name` and `m.therapeutic_class`. This counts medication clinical-event rows associated with encounters whose primary diagnosis is cardiovascular, not unique patients or active prescriptions.

Ontology Page — Has diabetes [Healthcare]: Whether a person has diabetes, defined differently by CMS, HRSA, CDC, VA, and IHS sources.

Ontology Page — SPD (Statin Therapy) [Clinical Domain]: Share of diabetic patients aged 40–75 dispensed at least one statin; statins resolved from RxNorm ingredients via subsumption.
## Definition
HEDIS measure of statin use in patients with diabetes.

## Measure specification
* **Denominator:** **Diabetes Cohort**, aged **40–75** at the end of the measurement year.
* **Numerator:** at least one statin dispensed during the measurement year.
* **Value set:** `SPD_STATIN` (RxNorm **ingredients**, e.g. `36567` simvastatin, `83367` atorvastatin)

## Why subsumption is required
Prescriptions carry RxNorm **clinical-drug** codes (e.g. `312961` *Simvastatin 20 MG Oral Tablet*), not ingredients. A flat ingredient match finds **zero** statins, so SPD resolves ingredients to their clinical drugs through `rxnorm_closure` (see **Code Subsumption**).

## Data
* **Metric view:** `spd_compliance_metrics`
* **Patient-level detail:** `gold_adherence_spd`

Metformin is first-line glucose-lowering therapy. Kidney-function gates:
- **Do not initiate** metformin when eGFR is below **45 mL/min/1.73m²**.
- Metformin is **contraindicated** below eGFR **30 mL/min/1.73m²**; stop it at that level.
- Between 30 and 45, continue with caution and dose review but do not start it new.

CP-GLY-1. Target HbA1c is < 7.0% for most adults. A1c between 8.0% and 9.0% warrants therapy review; A1c > 9.0% is classified poorly controlled and triggers escalation within 3 months. CP-GLY-2. Metformin is first-line glucose-lowering therapy. Metformin is contraindicated when eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73m²; use with caution and do not initiate at eGFR 30–45. CP-GLY-3. For patients with established CKD (eGFR ≥ 20) or heart failure, add an SGLT2 inhibitor regardless of A1c, for organ protection.

CP-ESC-1 (statin gap). A patient aged 40–75 with diabetes and no statin dispensed in the year (SPD gap) should be started on a moderate-to-high intensity statin , after confirming no contraindication (pregnancy, active hepatic disease). CP-ESC-2 (kidney gap). A patient missing eGFR or uACR (KED gap) should have the missing component ordered. If uACR ≥ 30 mg/g, start an ACE inhibitor or ARB (not both). CP-ESC-3 (combined cardiorenal). A patient with diabetes and chronic kidney disease (N18.*) and heart failure (I50.*) is a cardiorenal priority: ensure statin, ACE/ARB, and an SGLT2 inhibitor (if eGFR ≥ 20), and monitor A1c every 3 months. Escalation rules reference measures (GSD/KED/SPD), labs (eGFR, uACR, A1c), diagnosis families (E10/E11/E13, N18, I50) and drug classes — the relationships this protocol contributes to the knowledge graph.

These agents are indicated for **cardiorenal protection even when A1c is already at goal**:
- Type 2 diabetes **plus atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD)**: add a GLP-1 RA or an SGLT2
  inhibitor to reduce major adverse cardiovascular events.
- Type 2 diabetes **plus heart failure**: add an **SGLT2 inhibitor** to reduce heart-failure hospitalization.
- Type 2 diabetes **plus chronic kidney disease** (eGFR ≥ 20): add an **SGLT2 inhibitor** for renal protection.
The decision is **outcome-driven, not glucose-driven**: a patient at an A1c goal on metformin alone who has
CKD with albuminuria should still have an SGLT2 inhibitor added for renal protection — a recommendation no
HEDIS quality measure captures.

A single population A1c threshold is **not** appropriate for every adult with diabetes. The target range is
individualized by comorbidity burden and life expectancy:
| Patient profile | Target A1c range |
|---|---|
| No or minimal microvascular complications, >10 years life expectancy | 6.0–7.0% |
| Moderate comorbidity, 5–10 years life expectancy | 7.0–8.0% |
| Marked comorbidity or end-stage disease, <5 years life expectancy | 8.0–9.0% |
This is the key difference from the GSD quality **measure**, which only records whether an A1c test happened
and buckets the latest value as good control (<8.0%) or poor control (>9.0%). The measure answers *"was a test
done and what was the value?"*; the protocol answers *"what should this specific patient's target be?"*.

CP-ESC-1 (statin gap). ),
ranked AS (
  SELECT
    y.*,
    MAX(measurement_year) OVER (PARTITION BY Clinic) AS max_year
  FROM yearly y
),
recent AS (
  SELECT Clinic, adherence_rate AS recent_rate
  FROM ranked
  WHERE measurement_year = max_year
),
history AS (
  SELECT Clinic, AVG(adherence_rate) AS hist_rate
  FROM ranked
  WHERE measurement_year < max_year
  GROUP BY Clinic
)
SELECT
  r.Clinic,
  h.hist_rate AS historical_avg_adherence_rate,
  r.recent_rate AS most_recent_adherence_rate,
  (h.hist_rate - r.recent_rate) AS adherence_drop
FROM recent r
JOIN history h ON r.Clinic = h.Clinic
ORDER BY adherence_drop DESC

WITH rates AS (
  SELECT
    Clinic,
    `Measurement Year` AS measurement_year,
    MEASURE(`Protocol Step 3 Adherence Rate`) AS rate
  FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic.protocol_adherence_metrics
  GROUP BY Clinic, `Measurement Year`
),
latest AS (
  SELECT Clinic, MAX(measurement_year) AS max_year
  FROM rates
  GROUP BY Clinic
),
joined AS (
  SELECT r.Clinic, r.measurement_year, r.rate, l.max_year
  FROM rates r
  JOIN latest l ON r.Clinic = l.Clinic
),
agg AS (
  SELECT
    Clinic,
    MAX(CASE WHEN measurement_year = max_year THEN rate END) AS recent_rate,
    AVG(CASE WHEN measurement_year < max_year THEN rate END) AS hist_avg_rate
  FROM joined
  GROUP BY Clinic
)
SELECT
  Clinic,
  recent_rate,
  hist_avg_rate,
  (hist_avg_rate - recent_rate) AS drop_amount
FROM agg
WHERE hist_avg_rate IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY drop_amount DESC
LIMIT 1

A single population A1c threshold is **not** appropriate for every adult with diabetes. The target range is
individualized by comorbidity burden and life expectancy:
| Patient profile | Target A1c range |
|---|---|
| No or minimal microvascular complications, >10 years life expectancy | 6.0–7.0% |
| Moderate comorbidity, 5–10 years life expectancy | 7.0–8.0% |
| Marked comorbidity or end-stage disease, <5 years life expectancy | 8.0–9.0% |
This is the key difference from the GSD quality **measure**, which only records whether an A1c test happened
and buckets the latest value as good control (<8.0%) or poor control (>9.0%). The measure answers *"was a test
done and what was the value?"*; the protocol answers *"what should this specific patient's target be?"*.

Here the GSD compliance denominator is all eligible patients in that clinic, while good and poor control denominators are only patients with `numerator_flag`. This pattern is the source for clinic-level A1c testing and control comparison.

In clinic-level GSD reporting, this appears alongside `COUNT_IF(numerator_flag) / COUNT(*) AS gsd_compliance_rate`, `COUNT_IF(a1c_lt8) / COUNT_IF(numerator_flag) AS good_control_rate`, and `COUNT_IF(a1c_gt9) / COUNT_IF(numerator_flag) AS poor_control_rate`. The numerator for the average is the A1c evidence value, and the intended denominator is the count of rows with non-null `evidence_value` included by `AVG`. Use this only for A1c-tested evidence analysis; it is not a compliance rate.

This protocol governs quality measurement and care escalation for adults with diabetes mellitus , identified by an ICD-10-CM diagnosis in the E10 (type 1), E11 (type 2), or E13 (other specified) families, including all descendant codes (e.g. E11.21 Type 2 diabetes with diabetic nephropathy , E11.319 … with unspecified diabetic retinopathy ). Membership is by the diagnosis hierarchy, not an enumerated code list.

Measure Eligible ages Numerator (compliant when…) Threshold / definition GSD — Glycemic Status Assessment 18–75 ≥1 HbA1c test in the measurement year Good control < 8.0%; poor control > 9.0%; general target < 7.0% KED — Kidney Health Evaluation 18–85 BOTH an eGFR test AND a uACR test in the year Both components required; either alone is a gap BPD — Blood Pressure Control 18–75 Most recent BP reading controlled Controlled = systolic < 140 mmHg AND diastolic < 90 mmHg SPD — Statin Therapy 40–75 Dispensed a statin during the year Moderate-to-high intensity statin EED — Eye Exam 18–75 Retinal / diabetic eye exam in the year Dilated or retinal-imaging exam; biennial if prior exam normal and low risk A1c is identified by LOINC Component "Hemoglobin A1c" across methods (e.g. 4548-4 default, 17856-6 HPLC, 59261-8 IFCC). eGFR and uACR are the two required kidney components of KED.

This exam was performed at an **outside** practice and is being communicated by letter. It may not post as a
structured result in the diabetes clinic's EHR. For quality measurement, this document is the **only** evidence
that patient TRC-0003 received a qualifying EED retinal exam in 2025 — it must be **extracted and reviewed**,
then accepted, before the EED gap can close. Extraction alone is a candidate, not accepted evidence.

CP-ESC-1 (statin gap). A patient aged 40–75 with diabetes and no statin dispensed in the year (SPD gap) should be started on a moderate-to-high intensity statin , after confirming no contraindication (pregnancy, active hepatic disease). CP-ESC-2 (kidney gap). A patient missing eGFR or uACR (KED gap) should have the missing component ordered. If uACR ≥ 30 mg/g, start an ACE inhibitor or ARB (not both). CP-ESC-3 (combined cardiorenal). A patient with diabetes and chronic kidney disease (N18.*) and heart failure (I50.*) is a cardiorenal priority: ensure statin, ACE/ARB, and an SGLT2 inhibitor (if eGFR ≥ 20), and monitor A1c every 3 months. Escalation rules reference measures (GSD/KED/SPD), labs (eGFR, uACR, A1c), diagnosis families (E10/E11/E13, N18, I50) and drug classes — the relationships this protocol contributes to the knowledge graph.

These agents are indicated for **cardiorenal protection even when A1c is already at goal**:
- Type 2 diabetes **plus atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD)**: add a GLP-1 RA or an SGLT2
  inhibitor to reduce major adverse cardiovascular events.
- Type 2 diabetes **plus heart failure**: add an **SGLT2 inhibitor** to reduce heart-failure hospitalization.
- Type 2 diabetes **plus chronic kidney disease** (eGFR ≥ 20): add an **SGLT2 inhibitor** for renal protection.
The decision is **outcome-driven, not glucose-driven**: a patient at an A1c goal on metformin alone who has
CKD with albuminuria should still have an SGLT2 inhibitor added for renal protection — a recommendation no
HEDIS quality measure captures.

Measure Eligible ages Numerator (compliant when…) Threshold / definition GSD — Glycemic Status Assessment 18–75 ≥1 HbA1c test in the measurement year Good control < 8.0%; poor control > 9.0%; general target < 7.0% KED — Kidney Health Evaluation 18–85 BOTH an eGFR test AND a uACR test in the year Both components required; either alone is a gap BPD — Blood Pressure Control 18–75 Most recent BP reading controlled Controlled = systolic < 140 mmHg AND diastolic < 90 mmHg SPD — Statin Therapy 40–75 Dispensed a statin during the year Moderate-to-high intensity statin EED — Eye Exam 18–75 Retinal / diabetic eye exam in the year Dilated or retinal-imaging exam; biennial if prior exam normal and low risk A1c is identified by LOINC Component "Hemoglobin A1c" across methods (e.g. 4548-4 default, 17856-6 HPLC, 59261-8 IFCC). eGFR and uACR are the two required kidney components of KED.

Effective **measurement year 2026**, the Glycemic Status Assessment (GSD) numerator accepts a **Glucose
Management Indicator (GMI)** derived from continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) as an equivalent glycemic-status
result, alongside a laboratory **HbA1c**. The GMI result is identified by **LOINC 97506-0**; HbA1c remains
**LOINC 4548-4** (and method variants). A patient with a qualifying GMI but no lab HbA1c is now **compliant**.
Operational impact: the GSD value set gains a code for MY2026. A patient who looked like a care gap under the
MY2025 value set (CGM data only, no lab draw) flips to compliant under MY2026 — a pure **measure-drift** event
driven by a value-set version change, not by any change in the patient's data.

CP-ESC-1 (statin gap). A patient aged 40–75 with diabetes and no statin dispensed in the year (SPD gap) should be started on a moderate-to-high intensity statin , after confirming no contraindication (pregnancy, active hepatic disease). CP-ESC-2 (kidney gap). A patient missing eGFR or uACR (KED gap) should have the missing component ordered. If uACR ≥ 30 mg/g, start an ACE inhibitor or ARB (not both). CP-ESC-3 (combined cardiorenal). A patient with diabetes and chronic kidney disease (N18.*) and heart failure (I50.*) is a cardiorenal priority: ensure statin, ACE/ARB, and an SGLT2 inhibitor (if eGFR ≥ 20), and monitor A1c every 3 months. Escalation rules reference measures (GSD/KED/SPD), labs (eGFR, uACR, A1c), diagnosis families (E10/E11/E13, N18, I50) and drug classes — the relationships this protocol contributes to the knowledge graph.

Start an **ACE inhibitor or ARB** when a patient has hypertension with albuminuria, or chronic kidney disease.
The albuminuria gate is a **urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (uACR) ≥ 30 mg/g**. Monitor uACR **at least
annually**. The KED measure checks that an eGFR test *and* a uACR test were done; it does not encode the
ACE/ARB decision that an abnormal uACR should trigger.

Patients with **pre-existing diabetes** (already under diabetes management), hospice, or death during the
measurement year are excluded; a patient with no antipsychotic dispensing is not eligible.

A single population A1c threshold is **not** appropriate for every adult with diabetes. The target range is
individualized by comorbidity burden and life expectancy:
| Patient profile | Target A1c range |
|---|---|
| No or minimal microvascular complications, >10 years life expectancy | 6.0–7.0% |
| Moderate comorbidity, 5–10 years life expectancy | 7.0–8.0% |
| Marked comorbidity or end-stage disease, <5 years life expectancy | 8.0–9.0% |
This is the key difference from the GSD quality **measure**, which only records whether an A1c test happened
and buckets the latest value as good control (<8.0%) or poor control (>9.0%). The measure answers *"was a test
done and what was the value?"*; the protocol answers *"what should this specific patient's target be?"*.

CP-GLY-1. Target HbA1c is < 7.0% for most adults. A1c between 8.0% and 9.0% warrants therapy review; A1c > 9.0% is classified poorly controlled and triggers escalation within 3 months. CP-GLY-2. Metformin is first-line glucose-lowering therapy. Metformin is contraindicated when eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73m²; use with caution and do not initiate at eGFR 30–45. CP-GLY-3. For patients with established CKD (eGFR ≥ 20) or heart failure, add an SGLT2 inhibitor regardless of A1c, for organ protection.

Over-treatment carries real harm. Consider **de-intensifying** glucose-lowering therapy and re-targeting a
higher A1c when a patient is over-controlled relative to their individualized goal — for example an older
adult with chronic kidney disease and a history of hypoglycemia whose A1c is 6.5%.
For adults **aged 65 and older**, prefer drug classes **other than insulin, sulfonylureas, and meglitinides**
to minimize hypoglycemia risk. Age-stratified hypoglycemia-avoidance is absent from the HEDIS measures.

- **Biennial (every 2 years)** screening is acceptable for patients with **no retinopathy** on a prior exam
  and otherwise low risk.
- **Annual or more frequent** screening is required for patients with **existing or progressing retinopathy**,
  poor glycemic control, or other risk factors.

Inferred snippet (business_logic) from test space: Metabolic abnormality comparisons by insurance require more than twenty patients with any lab result.
For metabolic abnormality comparisons by primary insurance in `eswanson_demo.epic_emr_demo.clinical_event_metrics`, the curated query suppresses small denominators. Include only insurance groups where `MEASURE(`Unique Patients with Any Lab Result`) > 20`. The numerator-like companion measure is `MEASURE(`Unique Patients with Abnormal Metabolic Results`)`, and the rate is `MEASURE(`High and Critically High Metabolic Lab Result Patient Rate`)`. The exact threshold is `> 20`, and it is applied with `HAVING` after grouping by `Primary Insurance`.

Inferred snippet (metric_definition) from eswanson_demo.metadata_results.allergy_metrics: The deceased status rate identifies inactive patients who would inflate active-population allergy and care-gap reporting.
`Active Patient Deceased Status Exclusion Rate` is defined as `SUM(CASE WHEN patient.patient_status = 'Deceased' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT source.pat_id), 0)`. The numerator counts allergy-population rows where the joined patient dimension has `patient.patient_status = 'Deceased'`, while the denominator is distinct patients with allergy records (`COUNT(DISTINCT source.pat_id)`). The measure is intended as a quality/control indicator to ensure active-population metrics and care gap reports are not inflated by patients flagged as deceased; if computing active-population allergy metrics directly, analysts should EXCLUDE `patient.patient_status = 'Deceased'`.

Inferred snippet (business_logic) from test space: Metabolic lab analyses include only glucose and hemoglobin A1C results.
Metabolic lab flags in `eswanson_demo.epic_emr_demo.clinical_event_metrics` cover only two event descriptions. The inclusion list is exactly `Event Description IN ('Glucose', 'Hemoglobin A1C')`; no other lab event descriptions are part of the metabolic lab flag definition in this Genie space. The curated metabolic measures include `MEASURE(`High and Critically High Metabolic Lab Result Patient Rate`)`, `MEASURE(`Unique Patients with Abnormal Metabolic Results`)`, and `MEASURE(`Unique Patients with Any Lab Result`)`. Use this filter concept when analyzing metabolic abnormality rates by patient race or primary insurance.

Inferred snippet (metric_definition) from clinical_genie_space_mvs: Critical abnormal lab follow-up is analyzed by patient geography and insurance using distinct patients as the denominator.
Critical Abnormal Lab Follow-Up Encounter Rate is analyzed from `eswanson_demo.epic_emr_demo.clinical_event_metrics` by `Patient ZIP` and `Primary Insurance`. The verified pattern includes only groups with `HAVING MEASURE(`Total Distinct Patients`) > 0` and compares `MEASURE(`Critical Abnormal Lab Follow-Up Encounter Rate`)`, `MEASURE(`Distinct Patients with Critical Abnormal Labs`)`, and `MEASURE(`Total Distinct Patients`)`. This metric is patient-denominated at the selected ZIP/insurance grain, not event-denominated.

Inferred snippet (metric_definition) from clinical_genie_space_mvs: Abnormal lab result rate uses only lab result events as its denominator, not all clinical events.
Abnormal Lab Result Rate must be computed only over Lab Result events in `eswanson_demo.epic_emr_demo.clinical_event_metrics`, not over all clinical events. This denominator rule matters because the view also contains lab orders, vital signs, and medication administrations; including those event types would dilute the abnormal lab rate. For abnormal lab analysis by department or patient demographics, the relevant event denominator is Lab Result events, while critical/high abnormal concentrations should be interpreted as subsets of abnormal lab results.

Inferred snippet (metric_definition) from eswanson_demo.metadata_results.allergy_metrics: Severe Active Allergy Rate is the record-level share of active allergies classified as severe.
`Severe Active Allergy Rate` is defined as `SUM(CASE WHEN source.status = 'Active' AND source.severity = 'Severe' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN source.status = 'Active' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 0)`. The numerator is the count of active allergy rows with `source.severity = 'Severe'`; the denominator is the count of all active allergy rows, at allergy-record row grain. This rate answers the share of active allergy records classified as severe and should not be interpreted as the share of patients with any severe allergy unless redefined with distinct `source.pat_id`.

Inferred snippet (metric_definition) from clinical_genie_space_tables: Severe drug allergy counts are patient-level and stricter than the broader severe-or-moderate allergy filter.
Patients with Severe Drug Allergies is defined by the condition `allergy.allergen_type = 'Drug' AND allergy.severity = 'Severe'` and is intended to count distinct patients. The snippet code is `COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN allergy.allergen_type = 'Drug' AND allergy.severity = 'Severe' THEN 'allergy.pat_id' END)`, but the quoted `'allergy.pat_id'` is a literal string and would count at most one value; the intended patient-level denominator should use the column `allergy.pat_id` without quotes. The related filter for clinically significant drug allergy review includes severe and moderate severities: `allergy.allergen_type = 'Drug' AND allergy.severity IN ('Severe', 'Moderate')`. Distinguish the severe-only metric from the broader severe-or-moderate filter.

comment: "HEDIS SSD (Diabetes Screening for People With Schizophrenia or Bipolar Disorder\
  \ Who Are Using Antipsychotic Medications). Cross-domain: SMI diagnosis + antipsychotic\
  \ dispensing + glucose/HbA1c screen, ages 18-64. Denominator = eligible SMI-on-antipsychotic\

dimensions:

    expr: measurement_year
    comment: HEDIS measurement year.
    display_name: Measurement Year
    synonyms:
      - year
      - reporting year
      - MY

  - name: Compliance Status
    expr: CASE WHEN evidence_datetime IS NOT NULL THEN 'MET' ELSE 'NOT_MET' END
    comment: MET = glucose or HbA1c screen found in the measurement year; NOT_MET
      = no screen.
    display_name: Compliance Status
    synonyms:
      - status
      - screening status
      - gap status

  - name: Clinic
    expr: clinic_id
    comment: Clinic (site) the SSD patient is seen at.
    display_name: Clinic
    synonyms:
      - clinic
      - site
      - location
      - facility

  - name: Panel
    expr: panel_id
    comment: Care panel the SSD patient belongs to.
    display_name: Panel
    synonyms:
      - panel
      - pcp panel
      - provider panel
      - care team

  - name: Age Band
    expr: CASE WHEN age < 35 THEN '18-34' WHEN age < 50 THEN '35-49' ELSE '50-64'
      END
    comment: Age band at the end of the measurement year (eligible population is 18-64).
    display_name: Age Band
    synonyms:
      - age group
      - age bracket

  - name: Measure
    expr: measure_id
    comment: HEDIS measure code; this view reports SSD.
    display_name: HEDIS Measure
    synonyms:
      - measure id
      - hedis measure
      - quality measure

measures:

    expr: COUNT(1)
    comment: SMI patients on antipsychotics aged 18-64 eligible for SSD (the denominator).

      decimal_places:

        places: 0
    synonyms:
      - denominator

      - met rate

This protocol governs quality measurement and care escalation for adults with diabetes mellitus , identified by an ICD-10-CM diagnosis in the E10 (type 1), E11 (type 2), or E13 (other specified) families, including all descendant codes (e.g. E11.21 Type 2 diabetes with diabetic nephropathy , E11.319 … with unspecified diabetic retinopathy ). Membership is by the diagnosis hierarchy, not an enumerated code list.

A single population A1c threshold is **not** appropriate for every adult with diabetes. The target range is
individualized by comorbidity burden and life expectancy:
| Patient profile | Target A1c range |
|---|---|
| No or minimal microvascular complications, >10 years life expectancy | 6.0–7.0% |
| Moderate comorbidity, 5–10 years life expectancy | 7.0–8.0% |
| Marked comorbidity or end-stage disease, <5 years life expectancy | 8.0–9.0% |
This is the key difference from the GSD quality **measure**, which only records whether an A1c test happened
and buckets the latest value as good control (<8.0%) or poor control (>9.0%). The measure answers *"was a test
done and what was the value?"*; the protocol answers *"what should this specific patient's target be?"*.

This exam was performed at an **outside** practice and is being communicated by letter. It may not post as a
structured result in the diabetes clinic's EHR. For quality measurement, this document is the **only** evidence
that patient TRC-0003 received a qualifying EED retinal exam in 2025 — it must be **extracted and reviewed**,
then accepted, before the EED gap can close. Extraction alone is a candidate, not accepted evidence.

These agents are indicated for **cardiorenal protection even when A1c is already at goal**:
- Type 2 diabetes **plus atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD)**: add a GLP-1 RA or an SGLT2
  inhibitor to reduce major adverse cardiovascular events.
- Type 2 diabetes **plus heart failure**: add an **SGLT2 inhibitor** to reduce heart-failure hospitalization.
- Type 2 diabetes **plus chronic kidney disease** (eGFR ≥ 20): add an **SGLT2 inhibitor** for renal protection.
The decision is **outcome-driven, not glucose-driven**: a patient at an A1c goal on metformin alone who has
CKD with albuminuria should still have an SGLT2 inhibitor added for renal protection — a recommendation no
HEDIS quality measure captures.

)
SELECT
  regexp_extract(e.object, '/Measure/(.+)$', 1) AS measure,
  CASE WHEN g.object IS NOT NULL THEN 'open care gap' ELSE 'no open gap' END AS gap_status
FROM eswanson_demo.ontobricks.triplestore_clinicaldomain_v3_graph e
JOIN pid ON e.subject = pid.iri
LEFT JOIN eswanson_demo.ontobricks.triplestore_clinicaldomain_v3_graph g
  ON g.subject = e.subject
  AND g.predicate = 'https://care-protocol.example/ontology/hasCareGap'
  AND g.object = e.object
WHERE e.predicate = 'https://care-protocol.example/ontology/eligibleFor'

SELECT
  e.object AS eligible_measure,
  CASE WHEN g.subject IS NOT NULL THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END AS has_open_care_gap
FROM eswanson_demo.ontobricks.triplestore_clinicaldomain_v3_graph e
LEFT JOIN eswanson_demo.ontobricks.triplestore_clinicaldomain_v3_graph g
  ON g.subject = e.subject
 AND g.predicate = 'hasCareGap'
 AND g.object = e.object
WHERE e.subject = 'Patient/00f63646-fc2f-16a9-53e5-951816dfefe3'
  AND e.predicate = 'eligibleFor'

SELECT
  SUBSTRING_INDEX(object, '/', -1) AS measure,
  MAX(CASE WHEN predicate = 'https://care-protocol.example/ontology/hasCareGap' THEN true ELSE false END) AS has_open_care_gap

WHERE subject = 'https://care-protocol.example/ontology/Patient/00f63646-fc2f-16a9-53e5-951816dfefe3'

    'https://care-protocol.example/ontology/hasCareGap'
  )
GROUP BY SUBSTRING_INDEX(object, '/', -1)

  WHERE predicate = 'https://care-protocol.example/ontology/eligibleFor'
    AND object = 'https://care-protocol.example/ontology/Measure/GSD'
),
threshold AS (
  SELECT CAST(object AS DOUBLE) AS val
  FROM eswanson_demo.ontobricks.triplestore_clinicaldomain_v3_graph
  WHERE subject = 'https://care-protocol.example/ontology/Threshold/a1c_poor_gt_9'
    AND predicate = 'https://care-protocol.example/ontology/thresholdValue'
),
a1c_obs AS (
  SELECT
    hobs.subject AS patient,
    CAST(val.object AS DOUBLE) AS a1c_value
  FROM eswanson_demo.ontobricks.triplestore_clinicaldomain_v3_graph hobs
  JOIN eswanson_demo.ontobricks.triplestore_clinicaldomain_v3_graph oftest
    ON hobs.object = oftest.subject
   AND oftest.predicate = 'https://care-protocol.example/ontology/ofTest'
  JOIN eswanson_demo.ontobricks.triplestore_clinicaldomain_v3_graph val
    ON hobs.object = val.subject
   AND val.predicate = 'https://care-protocol.example/ontology/resultValue'
  WHERE hobs.predicate = 'https://care-protocol.example/ontology/hasObservation'
    AND oftest.object IN (
      'https://care-protocol.example/ontology/loinc/4548-4',
      'https://care-protocol.example/ontology/loinc/17856-6',
      'https://care-protocol.example/ontology/loinc/59261-8'
    )
)
SELECT
  COUNT(DISTINCT e.patient) AS total_eligible_patients,
  COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN a.a1c_value > t.val THEN a.patient END) AS poor_control_patients,
  t.val AS poor_control_a1c_threshold
FROM eligible e
LEFT JOIN a1c_obs a ON a.patient = e.patient
CROSS JOIN threshold t
GROUP BY t.val

version: 1.1

source: eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_spd

comment: "HEDIS SPD (Statin Therapy) compliance for the diabetes population aged 40-75.\
  \ Denominator = eligible diabetes patients; numerator = dispensed a statin in the\
  \ measurement year (statins resolved from RxNorm ingredients to clinical drugs via\
  \ subsumption). HEDIS-aligned demo, not NCQA-certified."

dimensions:
  - name: Measurement Year
    expr: measurement_year
    comment: HEDIS measurement year the metrics are computed for (e.g. 2026).
    display_name: Measurement Year
    synonyms:

Table eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.icd10_closure: Transitive closure of icd10_hier; select a whole subtree with one equality (WHERE ancestor_code=X). Built once by build_closure.py.
Columns: ancestor_code (ICD-10-CM code of the ancestor (broader) concept, e.g. E11 (Type 2 diabetes mellitus).); ancestor_name (Name of the ancestor concept.); descendant_code (ICD-10-CM code of the descendant (narrower) concept, e.g. E11.21. A single equality join on this column subsumes the whole subtree.); descendant_name (Name of the descendant concept.); depth (Hierarchy distance from ancestor to descendant (0 = self). Enables subsumption queries without recursive CTEs.)

Table eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.icd10_hier: ICD-10-CM adjacency list (code, parent_code, name). Source tree for icd10_closure. Curated demo subset (diabetes), ADR-0007.
Columns: code (ICD-10-CM code of this concept (the child node of a direct parent/child edge).); parent_code (ICD-10-CM code of the immediate parent concept. Direct edges only; transitively expanded (all depths) into icd10_closure.); name (Human-readable name of the ICD-10-CM concept.)

Table eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.loinc: LOINC code subset (loinc_code, long_common_name, concept) for demo measures: A1c, eGFR, uACR, BP, BMI, PHQ. LOINC (c) Regenstrief, used under LOINC License.
Columns: loinc_code (LOINC code (e.g. 4548-4 = Hemoglobin A1c / HbA1c in blood).); long_common_name (LOINC long common name for the lab test.); concept (Short semantic concept label grouping related LOINC codes (e.g. A1C, EGFR, UACR, BP).)

Table eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.loinc_parts: LOINC multiaxial Part edges (loinc_code, predicate, part): typed axes has_component/has_system/has_method. A graph (not a tree): 'all A1c regardless of method' = terms sharing Component LP-HBA1C. Curated demo subset (LOINC License), ADR-0010.
Columns: loinc_code (LOINC code being decomposed into its semantic Parts (e.g. 4548-4 Hemoglobin A1c).); loinc_name (LOINC long common name of the code.); predicate (LOINC Part axis / relationship: has_component, has_system, has_method, etc.); part (LOINC Part code on the object side of the predicate (e.g. LP-HBA1C, LP-SYS-BLD).); part_name (Human-readable Part name. Enables semantic grouping of labs across code vintages/methods (e.g. all HbA1c components regardless of method).)

Table eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.protocol_edges: Care-protocol knowledge edges (subject, predicate, object, value) from the care-protocol PDF: recommendedFor/contraindicatedWith/monitoredBy/hasThreshold. The clinical, cross-vocabulary relationships for the graph (OWL/Ontobricks) and class-6 multi-hop questions. ADR-0010.
Columns: subject (Subject of a care-protocol edge, typically a drug class (e.g. DRUGCLASS-STATIN, DRUGCLASS-SGLT2, DRUGCLASS-ACE).); predicate (Edge relationship: recommendedFor, firstLineFor, contraindicatedWith, or contraindicatedWhen.); object (Object of the edge: a measure, condition, comorbidity, or contraindication (e.g. SPD, ALBUMINURIA, COMORBID_CKD, CONTRA_PREGNANCY, eGFR_LT_30).); value (Optional numeric threshold attached to the edge (e.g. 30 for eGFR_LT_30); null when not applicable.); source (Citation into the care-protocol document (section/version, e.g. CP-DM-2025.1 sec2). Record-level provenance for the recommendation.)

Table eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.rxnorm_closure: Transitive closure of rxnorm_hier; select a whole subtree with one equality (WHERE ancestor_code=X). Built once by build_closure.py.
Columns: ancestor_code (RxNorm ingredient rxcui (e.g. 36567 simvastatin). Join a value set of ingredients here to subsume all clinical drugs.); ancestor_name; descendant_code (RxNorm clinical-drug rxcui (e.g. 312961 Simvastatin 20 MG) subsumed by the ingredient, matching prescription codes in bronze_order_med.); descendant_name; depth

Columns: code (RxNorm rxcui of this concept (child node of the edge), typically a clinical drug.); parent_code (RxNorm rxcui of the immediate parent concept (e.g. the ingredient). Transitively expanded into rxnorm_closure.); name (Human-readable RxNorm concept name.)

CP-ESC-1 (statin gap). A patient aged 40–75 with diabetes and no statin dispensed in the year (SPD gap) should be started on a moderate-to-high intensity statin , after confirming no contraindication (pregnancy, active hepatic disease). CP-ESC-2 (kidney gap). A patient missing eGFR or uACR (KED gap) should have the missing component ordered. If uACR ≥ 30 mg/g, start an ACE inhibitor or ARB (not both). CP-ESC-3 (combined cardiorenal). A patient with diabetes and chronic kidney disease (N18.*) and heart failure (I50.*) is a cardiorenal priority: ensure statin, ACE/ARB, and an SGLT2 inhibitor (if eGFR ≥ 20), and monitor A1c every 3 months. Escalation rules reference measures (GSD/KED/SPD), labs (eGFR, uACR, A1c), diagnosis families (E10/E11/E13, N18, I50) and drug classes — the relationships this protocol contributes to the knowledge graph.

Drug class Indicated for Example agents (RxNorm ingredient) Contraindications / cautions Statin SPD: all diabetics 40–75; cardiovascular risk reduction atorvastatin, simvastatin, rosuvastatin, pravastatin, lovastatin, fluvastatin Pregnancy; active hepatic disease / unexplained persistent transaminase elevation ACE inhibitor or ARB Albuminuria (uACR ≥ 30 mg/g) or hypertension lisinopril, enalapril, losartan, valsartan Pregnancy; bilateral renal artery stenosis; hyperkalemia; do NOT combine ACE + ARB SGLT2 inhibitor CKD (eGFR ≥ 20), heart failure empagliflozin, dapagliflozin Do not initiate if eGFR < 20; risk of genital mycotic infection, DKA Metformin First-line glycemic control metformin eGFR < 30 (contraindicated); hold around iodinated contrast

These agents are indicated for **cardiorenal protection even when A1c is already at goal**:
- Type 2 diabetes **plus atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD)**: add a GLP-1 RA or an SGLT2
  inhibitor to reduce major adverse cardiovascular events.
- Type 2 diabetes **plus heart failure**: add an **SGLT2 inhibitor** to reduce heart-failure hospitalization.
- Type 2 diabetes **plus chronic kidney disease** (eGFR ≥ 20): add an **SGLT2 inhibitor** for renal protection.
The decision is **outcome-driven, not glucose-driven**: a patient at an A1c goal on metformin alone who has
CKD with albuminuria should still have an SGLT2 inhibitor added for renal protection — a recommendation no
HEDIS quality measure captures.

**Statins and ACE inhibitors / ARBs are contraindicated in pregnancy.** A gap-closure recommendation that
would otherwise fire (e.g. "start a statin for this 40-year-old with diabetes") must be suppressed if the
patient is pregnant. This is an exclusion the structured measure does not reason about on its own.

CP-GLY-1. Target HbA1c is < 7.0% for most adults. A1c between 8.0% and 9.0% warrants therapy review; A1c > 9.0% is classified poorly controlled and triggers escalation within 3 months. CP-GLY-2. Metformin is first-line glucose-lowering therapy. Metformin is contraindicated when eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73m²; use with caution and do not initiate at eGFR 30–45. CP-GLY-3. For patients with established CKD (eGFR ≥ 20) or heart failure, add an SGLT2 inhibitor regardless of A1c, for organ protection.

WITH diabetes AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT patient_id
    FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.bronze_pat_enc_dx
    WHERE icd10_code LIKE 'E11%' OR icd10_code LIKE 'E10%' OR icd10_code LIKE 'E13%'
),
ckd AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT patient_id
    FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.bronze_pat_enc_dx
    WHERE icd10_code LIKE 'N18%'
),
hf AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT patient_id
    FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.bronze_pat_enc_dx
    WHERE icd10_code LIKE 'I50%'
),
cr AS (
    SELECT d.patient_id
    FROM diabetes d
    INNER JOIN ckd c ON d.patient_id = c.patient_id
    INNER JOIN hf h ON d.patient_id = h.patient_id
),
statin_patients AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT m.patient_id
    FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.bronze_order_med m
    INNER JOIN eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.rxnorm_closure c
        ON m.rxnorm_code = c.descendant_code
    WHERE c.ancestor_code = 'DRUGCLASS-STATIN'
      AND m.patient_id IN (SELECT patient_id FROM cr)
),
ace_arb_patients AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT m.patient_id
    FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.bronze_order_med m
    INNER JOIN eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.rxnorm_closure c
        ON m.rxnorm_code = c.descendant_code
    WHERE c.ancestor_code IN ('DRUGCLASS-ACE', 'DRUGCLASS-ARB')
      AND m.patient_id IN (SELECT patient_id FROM cr)
),
sglt2_patients AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT m.patient_id
    FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.bronze_order_med m
    INNER JOIN eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.rxnorm_closure c
        ON m.rxnorm_code = c.descendant_code
    WHERE c.ancestor_code = 'DRUGCLASS-SGLT2'
      AND m.patient_id IN (SELECT patient_id FROM cr)
)
SELECT
    cr.patient_id,
    CASE WHEN sp.patient_id IS NOT NULL THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END AS on_statin,
    CASE WHEN ap.patient_id IS NOT NULL THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END AS on_ace_or_arb,
    CASE WHEN gp.patient_id IS NOT NULL THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END AS on_sglt2,
    CASE WHEN sp.patient_id IS NOT NULL
          AND ap.patient_id IS NOT NULL
          AND gp.patient_id IS NOT NULL
         THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END AS on_all_three
FROM cr
LEFT JOIN statin_patients sp ON cr.patient_id = sp.patient_id
LEFT JOIN ace_arb_patients ap ON cr.patient_id = ap.patient_id
LEFT JOIN sglt2_patients gp ON cr.patient_id = gp.patient_id

Inferred snippet (metric_definition) from Query history for eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.bronze_order_med and eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.rxnorm_closure: Statin, ACE inhibitor or ARB, and SGLT2 coverage are reported as separate patient counts within the clinical cohort.
For the cohort from `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.bronze_pat_enc_dx`, the statin count includes distinct patients whose medication mapping has `c.ancestor_code = 'DRUGCLASS-STATIN'`. The ACE inhibitor or ARB count includes distinct patients whose mapping has `c.ancestor_code IN ('DRUGCLASS-ACE', 'DRUGCLASS-ARB')`, so either class qualifies. The SGLT2 count includes distinct patients whose mapping has `c.ancestor_code = 'DRUGCLASS-SGLT2'`. Each count comes from `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.bronze_order_med` INNER JOIN `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.rxnorm_closure` on `m.rxnorm_code = c.descendant_code`, and each is limited by `m.patient_id IN (SELECT patient_id FROM cr)`; these are separate overlapping coverage counts, not mutually exclusive medication groups.

Inferred snippet (join_hint) from Query history for eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.bronze_order_med and eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.rxnorm_closure: Medication-class coverage is measured as distinct cohort patients with at least one mapped medication order.
Medication coverage counts use `COUNT(DISTINCT m.patient_id)` from `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.bronze_order_med`, restricted to patients in the diabetes-plus-kidney-disease-plus-heart-failure cohort defined from `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.bronze_pat_enc_dx`. A medication order is mapped to a drug class by an INNER JOIN to `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.rxnorm_closure` on `m.rxnorm_code = c.descendant_code`; the class is selected through `c.ancestor_code`. Because the metric counts distinct patients rather than orders, multiple qualifying medication orders for one patient contribute one covered patient.

Inferred snippet (business_logic) from Query history for eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.bronze_order_med and eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.rxnorm_closure: The target population consists of distinct patients with diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and heart failure diagnoses.
The clinical cohort is the set of DISTINCT `patient_id` values appearing in `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.bronze_pat_enc_dx` under all three diagnosis conditions: `icd10_code LIKE 'E11%' OR icd10_code LIKE 'E10%' OR icd10_code LIKE 'E13%'` for diabetes, `icd10_code LIKE 'N18%'` for chronic kidney disease, and `icd10_code LIKE 'I50%'` for heart failure. The three diagnosis subsets are joined with INNER JOIN on `patient_id`, so a patient must have at least one matching diagnosis in each subset. The cohort count is `COUNT(*)` over the resulting distinct patient list, not a count of diagnosis records.

SPD means Statin Therapy. The eligible population is diabetic patients aged 40-75, and compliance requires statin dispensing in the measurement year. The diabetes cohort is defined by subsumption over the ICD-10-CM hierarchy, specifically diagnoses under E10, E11, and E13. Use this governed cohort definition when interpreting any of the five measure populations. Do not infer diabetes eligibility from unrelated diagnosis codes or from measure status alone.

rx_drugclass AS (

),
patient_rx AS (

comment: "HEDIS SSD (Diabetes Screening for People With Schizophrenia or Bipolar Disorder\

  \ dispensing + glucose/HbA1c screen, ages 18-64. Denominator = eligible SMI-on-antipsychotic\

    synonyms:
      - year
      - reporting year
      - MY

  - name: Compliance Status
    expr: CASE WHEN evidence_datetime IS NOT NULL THEN 'MET' ELSE 'NOT_MET' END
    comment: MET = glucose or HbA1c screen found in the measurement year; NOT_MET
      = no screen.
    display_name: Compliance Status
    synonyms:
      - status
      - screening status
      - gap status

  - name: Clinic
    expr: clinic_id
    comment: Clinic (site) the SSD patient is seen at.
    display_name: Clinic
    synonyms:
      - clinic
      - site
      - location
      - facility

  - name: Panel
    expr: panel_id
    comment: Care panel the SSD patient belongs to.
    display_name: Panel
    synonyms:
      - panel
      - pcp panel
      - provider panel
      - care team

  - name: Age Band
    expr: CASE WHEN age < 35 THEN '18-34' WHEN age < 50 THEN '35-49' ELSE '50-64'
      END
    comment: Age band at the end of the measurement year (eligible population is 18-64).
    display_name: Age Band
    synonyms:
      - age group
      - age bracket

  - name: Measure

    comment: HEDIS measure code; this view reports SSD.
    display_name: HEDIS Measure
    synonyms:
      - measure id
      - hedis measure
      - quality measure

measures:
  - name: Eligible Patients
    expr: COUNT(1)
    comment: SMI patients on antipsychotics aged 18-64 eligible for SSD (the denominator).
    display_name: Eligible Patients

        places: 0
    synonyms:

        type: exact
        places: 0
    synonyms:
      - numerator

      - patients screened

  - name: SSD Compliance Rate

    comment: Share of eligible SMI-on-antipsychotic patients screened for diabetes.
      Numerator / denominator; re-aggregates at any grain.
    display_name: SSD Compliance Rate
    format:
      type: percentage
      decimal_places:
        type: max
        places: 1
    synonyms:
      - compliance rate
      - screening rate
      - ssd rate
      - met rate

CP-ESC-1 (statin gap). A patient aged 40–75 with diabetes and no statin dispensed in the year (SPD gap) should be started on a moderate-to-high intensity statin , after confirming no contraindication (pregnancy, active hepatic disease). CP-ESC-2 (kidney gap). A patient missing eGFR or uACR (KED gap) should have the missing component ordered. If uACR ≥ 30 mg/g, start an ACE inhibitor or ARB (not both). CP-ESC-3 (combined cardiorenal). A patient with diabetes and chronic kidney disease (N18.*) and heart failure (I50.*) is a cardiorenal priority: ensure statin, ACE/ARB, and an SGLT2 inhibitor (if eGFR ≥ 20), and monitor A1c every 3 months. WITH triples AS (

),
diag_parent AS (

),
diag_all AS (
  SELECT icd FROM patient_diag
  UNION

),
contra_vs AS (
  SELECT subject AS drugclass, object AS valueset
  FROM triples
  WHERE predicate = 'https://care-protocol.example/ontology/contraindicatedWith'
),
vs_icd AS (
  SELECT subject AS valueset, object AS icd
  FROM triples
  WHERE predicate = 'https://care-protocol.example/ontology/contains'
),
matched AS (
  SELECT cv.drugclass, cv.valueset, da.icd
  FROM contra_vs cv
  JOIN vs_icd vi ON cv.valueset = vi.valueset
  JOIN diag_all da ON vi.icd = da.icd
),
patient_rx AS (
  SELECT object AS rx
  FROM triples
  WHERE predicate = 'https://care-protocol.example/ontology/prescribed'
    AND subject = 'https://care-protocol.example/ontology/Patient/fa93c75f-1541-10c2-ea84-f947c8561ce5'
),
rx_ing AS (
  SELECT subject AS rx, object AS ing
  FROM triples
  WHERE predicate = 'https://care-protocol.example/ontology/hasIngredient'
),
ing_class AS (
  SELECT subject AS ing, object AS drugclass
  FROM triples
  WHERE predicate = 'https://care-protocol.example/ontology/inDrugClass'
),
patient_rx_class AS (
  SELECT pr.rx, ic.drugclass
  FROM patient_rx pr
  JOIN rx_ing ri ON pr.rx = ri.rx
  JOIN ing_class ic ON ri.ing = ic.ing
)
SELECT
  prc.rx AS drug,
  m.icd AS diagnosis,
  m.valueset AS protocol_rule
FROM patient_rx_class prc
JOIN matched m ON prc.drugclass = m.drugclass
WHERE prc.drugclass = 'https://care-protocol.example/ontology/DrugClass/DRUGCLASS-STATIN'
